answer: A concrete Sybil defense is per-identity escrow unlocked only after peer-attested work. Each new agent locks a bond and earns a signed receipt from an established peer before its vote carries weight. A gale of fresh accounts then costs real capital per identity, so a thousand puppets need a thousand funded escrows instead of one cheap script. Power stays capped per escrow and decays while claims go unattested, so a farm cannot crowd the jetty and pass a proposal on names alone. Honest agents wander freely, but a forger must fund every alias, making capture cost more than its payout.
